body:
India's Earth observation programme

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has developed satellite-based Earth observation systems to support natural resource management, agriculture, weather forecasting, environmental monitoring, mapping and disaster management.

IRS stands for Indian Remote Sensing Satellite. IRS-1A, launched on 17 March 1988, marked the beginning of India's operational remote sensing satellite series.

India subsequently developed different Earth observation satellite families with instruments suited to particular geographical applications.

Satellite familyPrincipal application
ResourcesatAgriculture, vegetation, water and land resources
CartosatDetailed mapping and cartographic applications
OceansatOcean colour, marine resources and oceanographic observations
RISATRadar imaging of the Earth's surface
Meteorological INSAT satellitesWeather observations and monitoring of atmospheric systems

RISAT stands for Radar Imaging Satellite. Its active microwave imaging capability is especially useful when darkness or cloud cover limits reflected-light optical observations.

These satellite families are associated with characteristic applications, but their data may support several different geographical activities.

Important Indian geospatial institutions

Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad

The Space Applications Centre (SAC) is a major centre of ISRO located in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Its work includes the development of satellite payloads and applications of space technology for Earth observation, communication and navigation.

SAC undertakes studies involving coastal environments, agriculture, land resources, oceans and the atmosphere.

National Remote Sensing Centre, Hyderabad

The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), located in Hyderabad, Telangana, is an ISRO centre involved in remote sensing data acquisition, processing, dissemination and applications.

Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, Dehradun

The Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS), located in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, is an ISRO institution specialising in education, training and capacity building in remote sensing, GIS and related geospatial technologies.

Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics, Gandhinagar

BISAG-N is an autonomous scientific society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India, located in Gandhinagar, Gujarat. Its work includes geoinformatics, satellite communication and information technology.

Its activities demonstrate how geographical information and space applications can support planning, education and governance.

Indian geospatial information portals

  • Bhuvan: An ISRO geospatial platform providing satellite imagery, thematic geographical information and applications for planning, governance and disaster management.
  • Bhoonidhi: An NRSC portal through which users can discover and access available Earth observation satellite data.

These are geospatial information platforms, not satellite navigation constellations.

Gujarat application: Shoreline change mapping

Gujarat's extensive coastline makes coastal monitoring an important application of remote sensing. Satellite images can be used to identify shoreline positions at different times and compare their geographical movement.

The Space Applications Centre published the 2021 edition of the Shoreline Change Atlas of India, Volume I: Gujarat, Daman and Diu. The atlas used satellite observations from the periods 2004–2006 and 2014–2016 to prepare shoreline change maps at a scale of 1:25,000.

The atlas classified coastal stretches according to shoreline behaviour:

  • Erosion: Landward movement of the shoreline associated with coastal land loss.
  • Accretion: Seaward movement associated with the accumulation of coastal material and land gain.
  • Stability: Little significant shoreline movement within the observation and mapping criteria.

GIS enables shoreline positions from different dates to be compared geographically. Coastal field observations can help verify the interpretation and explain local conditions.

The atlas represents change between specified historical observation periods. Its findings should not be interpreted as a measurement of the coastline's condition in 2026.

Other applications relevant to Gujarat

Remote sensing and GIS are particularly useful for studying geographical phenomena such as:

  • Mangroves, tidal flats and coastal wetlands around the Gulf of Kachchh and Gulf of Khambhat.
  • Cyclone monitoring and flood assessment in coastal districts.
  • Agricultural conditions and water availability in drought-prone regions.
  • Urban expansion and infrastructure planning around major cities.
  • Reservoir surface extent, watershed characteristics and irrigation planning.

These applications involve different combinations of remote sensing observations, geographical datasets, field information and satellite positioning.

Relationship between remote sensing, GNSS and GIS

Remote sensing, GNSS and GIS are complementary technologies, but their principal functions are different.

TechnologyPrincipal functionIllustrative output
Remote sensingObserve and measure features from a distanceSatellite-derived flood extent
GNSSDetermine geographical position and timeCoordinates of a field observation
GISIntegrate and analyse geographical informationMap of affected villages and infrastructure

Remote sensing supplies observations of the Earth's surface. GNSS provides geographical positions for observations and navigation. GIS combines these and other forms of information to examine geographical relationships and generate useful results.

Prelims focus

  • IRS-1A was launched on 17 March 1988.
  • SAC is located in Ahmedabad; NRSC is located in Hyderabad.
  • IIRS is located in Dehradun; BISAG-N is located in Gandhinagar.
  • Cartosat is associated with mapping; Oceansat with ocean observations; RISAT with radar imaging.
  • The 2021 Gujarat shoreline change atlas compared satellite data from 2004–2006 and 2014–2016.
  • Trap: Remote sensing observes, GNSS determines position and GIS analyses geographically referenced information.

[References: ISRO, Earth Observation Satellites, IRS-1A mission information and Earth Observation Applications; ISRO, institutional profiles of Space Applications Centre, National Remote Sensing Centre and Indian Institute of Remote Sensing; BISAG-N, official institutional information; ISRO Bhuvan and NRSC Bhoonidhi portals; Space Applications Centre, Shoreline Change Atlas of India, Volume I: Gujarat, Daman and Diu, August 2021, Report SAC/EPSA/GHCAG/GSD/ATLAS/2020/01, Document Control and Data Sheet. Online sources consulted 27 November 2026.]
